newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Brierley rebuff by Fairfax confirmed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Brierley rebuff by Fairfax confirmed.

text.p: Publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd on Monday released results of a vote taken at general meeting on Friday that confirmed shareholders had rejected a plan by Brierley Investments Ltd to immediately increase its Fairfax stake to 25 percent from 20 percent.
On Friday, proxies from Fairfax shareholders showed a majority opposed the plan, but votes from the floor had not been counted.
A show of hands was overwhelmingly against the purchase.

Brierley agreed last December to buy Canadian media baron Conrad Black's 25 percent stake in Fairfax for A$447.1 million, but Australian company law forces anyone wanting more than 20 percent of a company to obtain shareholder approval or launch a full takeover bid.

But Brierley executive director Rodney Price, who was also elected to the Fairfax board at the meeting, said later on Friday Brierley would go ahead anyway with its plans to lift its stake to 25 percent using the "creep" provisions to buy three percent every six months.

The net effect of a confirmed shareholder rejection of Brierley's plan would be to increase the acquisition price for the remaining five percent and deliver Black's Hollinger Inc a small extra profit.
Brierley agreed to buy the shares from Hollinger at A$2.82 a share.
To buy the extra five percent from the market rather than Black over the next six months would add about A$15 million to the cost of the stake at current prices.
Conversely Hollinger stands to gain that much by selling the stake into the market at current prices.
Fairfax's shares closed up three cents at A$3.17 on Monday.
